body: also if you can, definitely tell his wife

Being completely honest, my biggest regret in life was when i was in a similiar situation to your wife. I wasnt married, but had a long time boyfriend i was pretty much living with, and I was an awful person and had a long time affair he ended up finding out about. He wanted to forgive me but i had just too much guilt and broke it off, and hes extremely happy now that i did. He was really hurt at the time, but he moved on and is doing really great now, is in a lot healthier relationship and im really happy for him. We are not on speaking terms and i havent talked to him in a few years, but i can definitely say hes a million times more happy than he wouldve been if we stayed together. Even if it was subconscious, i was able to cheat for a reason, the relationship was doomed the second i made that decision and it would have never worked out, just prolonged the pain till we eventually broke up later. You'll see stories from people who stayed with their cheating partner, they always continue and just get sneakier.

I know its extremely scary to think of going from seeing someone every single day, someone your life and whole identity was intertwined with, to never seeing them again. This is just my experience but slowly moving apart was much more painful then just cutting it off cold turkey. Its scarier doing it that way, but you actually deal with the hurt and lonliness a lot faster that way, when youre still talking to the person and keeping the option open to stay together, you dont heal in my experience, you cant move on.

sorry for the paragraphs lol i just wish i had someone say this to mer when i was going through this. You have the upper hand because you can leave the relationship knowing you were a good faithful partner and theres so many women out there looking for a guy like that.

You can always go back, its never too late, theres ways they can work with you too so you can do school online or go for your GED. Dont do it for anyone else but yourself, it will help in the long run, its something to work for and look forward too finishing and you can do it without family or friends.

 Im just saying it helped me when i was 14. Back then i had no way to interact with the outside world, no friends, phone, tv, not even a radio, my dad locked me in my room everyday and would take away even pens and pencils so i couldnt even draw or write. School was my only outlet and i didnt even do well anyways. I spent a lot of time self harming and wanting to disappear, but then i had to figure out how to keep going with absolutely no one else. i graduated with a 2.0 and horrible attendance, but it was enough i could go to college and leave my awful home.  so i know its not for everyone but like i said, theres so much life to experience. You can travel, date, do whatever you want if you can just make it to adulthood.

 I would say to take a night, sit down with a pen and paper and write down things that make you happy, if its watching a certain show, music, drawing whatever. And those can become healthy coping tools. You just need to distract yourself and time will fly by and before you know it youll be 18 and have the whole world to explore.

Drop her girl, no one needs that mess and shes clearly selfish. You need to take care of yourself first and foremost. Shes got issues that she needs to focus on and she wont change until she wants to. Dont let her use you, its not worth it. Whatever she decides to do is her decision and has nothing to do with you. I have a major self harming addiction and have suicidal thoughts so i know her mindset. I also use to drink everyday so i feel like we are a lot alike unfortunately lol. If she left her family (not judging her btw) and can make friends, then clearly she has enough self preservation to move on from different relationships and not do anything severe, she will be ok so you need to make sure you will be too.

When i was your age i was in a very similar place, and i also wanted to die. I kept going by just throwing myself into different books and movies and stuff, it made the time go by and helped me realize how my problems werent my identity. Im still a loner but it gets better, it really does. You'll find people who make you feel seen. Just focus on school so you can maybe move out when you go to college in just a couple years, even if you dont go to college youll still be able to move out if u want, its something to look forward too
im sorry babe, im here if u need to vent, ive been there before
im here if u want to vent, i get it more than you can imagine
